seoTitle: How to Search for a Word in Google Docs (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Search for words in Google Docs with a quick keyboard shortcut, then use Find and Replace with match-case rules to update text across the whole file.
intro: Scanning a long document manually for a specific word wastes time you don't need to spend. This guide covers activating the basic search bar with a keyboard shortcut, stepping through highlighted matches, and using the advanced Find and Replace tool to update text globally with rules like match case for precision.

steps.heading: Open the search bar
steps.body: Press Control+F or Command+F to instantly bring up the search field on desktop.

steps.heading: Step through matches
steps.body: Use the navigation arrows in the search results to jump directly between highlighted word instances across your pages.

steps.heading: Open Find and Replace
steps.body: Access the advanced wizard from the Edit menu to unlock more comprehensive search and replacement options.

steps.heading: Set specialized search rules
steps.body: Enable options like Match case or Match using regular expressions to isolate precise text strings.

steps.heading: Replace text globally or individually
steps.body: Use Replace for single instances or Replace all to update repeated text across the entire document with one command.

steps.heading: Search on mobile
steps.body: The Google Docs mobile app on Android and iOS also includes a built-in search tool for locating words on the go.

faq.question: What's the keyboard shortcut to search in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Press Control+F on Windows/ChromeOS or Command+F on macOS to open the search bar instantly.

faq.question: How do I replace every instance of a word at once?
faq.answer: Open Find and Replace from the Edit menu, enter your search and replacement terms, and use Replace all to update every match.

faq.question: Can I search for exact case matches only?
faq.answer: Yes, enable the Match case option in Find and Replace to restrict results to text matching your exact capitalization.

faq.question: Is search available in the mobile app?
faq.answer: Yes, the Google Docs app for Android and iOS includes a built-in search tool for finding words within a document.
